source.title: Emergent and Subliminal Misalignment Through the Lens of Data-Mediated Transfer
source.authors: Baris Askin; Muhammed Ustaomeroglu; Anupam Nayak; Gauri Joshi; Guan-Nan Qu; Carlee Joe-Wong

page_placements.theme: Teacher as scorer or logit source: on-policy and logit distillation transmit traits

record.tranche_reason: The study tests subliminal transfer using filtered teacher-generated, benign data and measures student misalignment, as in the original SFT setup. It also compares additional distillation channels and data distributions.
record.gate_note: The paper's direct emergent-misalignment experiments are not teacher-to-student subliminal-transfer tests. Mechanism accounts mentioned from other papers are citations, not this study's results. Rows focus on the study's own subliminal-transfer rates and comparisons.
record.test_reason: Same-base students are SFT'd (and logit-distilled) on misaligned-teacher outputs that a judge filtered to be aligned, and student misalignment (EM rate) is measured. This tests transmission (A) and harmful-trait transmission (C) in a new setting. The data are natural-language advice, tutoring, critique and summary responses on broad prompts, not numbers or code, and the paper adds distillation channels. Hence T3 rather than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Additionally, the authors conclude that token-level OPD transmits misalignment more strongly than SFT and near OPTD, and online filtering does not stop it. They also find that aligned teachers subliminally restore alignment near base levels, an asymmetry with misalignment transfer. They frame subliminal transfer as teacher-directed and data-gated.
record.recipe_differences: Uses shared corresponding base initialization, a narrowly misaligned teacher, benign Broad-NL-Dataset generations filtered by an LLM judge, and student EM evaluation. Unlike the original study's focus, it also compares full-vocabulary off-policy and token-level on-policy distillation, and does not test favourite-animal traits.
record.method_sensitivity: Training channel, teacher task/domain, and transfer-data prompt distribution affect reported rates. Broad-NL-Dataset yields substantially higher rates than MATH. Online filtering in OPD does not substantially change its rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Misalignment transfers under on-policy reverse-KL distillation on student rollouts, often exceeding SFT and approaching OPTD. Online filtering of rollouts does not reduce it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subliminal transfer via on-policy distillation: a misaligned teacher scoring only student-sampled tokens transmits misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Under logit distillation, transfer persists when trajectories come from the aligned base or other model families (Tables 14-16) or MATH gold answers (Table 13: 21.8%). The transfer pattern follows the teacher, not the data source (Tables 5, 17-20).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In full-vocabulary distillation, the teacher's distribution, not trajectory content, sets the direction of transferred misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Aligned teachers reverse narrow misalignment to near-base EM via SFT, OPTD and OPD on Broad-NL data, and via OPTD even on the original unsafe data (Fig 5, Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Teacher-mediated realignment is broader and easier than teacher-mediated misalignment transfer.

record.problems: Evaluation depends on LLM judges; the authors report manual validation on a sampled subset and note that different judges or rubrics may shift absolute rates. Results use LoRA rank 32 and 7B–14B models; there is no different-base comparison or full-fine-tuning/rank sweep. Numerical uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted the reported overall mean rows for Llama-3.1-8B and Olmo-3-7B-Instruct; domain-aggregated rates; detailed per-cell transfer matrices; and additional data-generator/teacher-pair comparisons in Tables 5 and 14–20. Those tables report further subliminal-transfer results and are identified in Sections 4.3 and E.2–E.5.

untested.parts: Favourite-animal or other preference traits; numbers or code as the transfer medium. Maths reasoning only via the MATH comparison, under SFT/OPTD on Llama-3.1-8B.
Entirely. Student and KL-target teacher always share a base. Tables 14-15 vary only the data-generating model under logit distillation from a same-base teacher.
Alignment-relevant traits other than narrow-to-broad EM misalignment.
Entirely. Divergence tokens are invoked only as a speculative explanation for MATH vs Broad-NL; no mechanistic test.
Full fine-tuning and other LoRA ranks (rank 32 only).

missing.what: Overall averages for Llama-3.1-8B (SFT 29.8, OPD 41.2, OPTD 39.9; teacher 52.1) and Olmo-3-7B (SFT 26.3, OPD 36.5, OPTD 36.0; teacher 46.5)
Teacher EM rates per task as upper comparator for each model (e.g. Qwen Adv 62.3, Sum 20.4, Tut 71.4, Crit 48.1)
MATH condition as separate rows with base-model 6.7% baseline; misaligned teacher avg 83.3%
Per-epoch SFT/OPTD EM (e.g. Llama SFT 31.9/33.0/33.5) showing saturation by epoch 2
OPTD on MATH teacher generations (28.0%) vs MATH ground-truth answers (21.8%)

record.verdict_notes: No control trains the student on base or aligned-teacher outputs on the same Broad-NL prompts. EM elevation over base therefore rests on the 6.7% Llama base rate. Section 3 shows benign fine-tuning moves EM, so a generic fine-tuning effect is not fully excluded. Transfer data are natural-language responses on advice-style prompts close to the EM evaluation tasks, not semantically distant numbers. The reader's 'controls: y' is generous. The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests misalignment transfer with benign Broad-NL-Dataset outputs filtered by a judge, not favourite-animal transmission or number/code/maths-reasoning outputs. The same-base setup is held fixed.
No different-base student/teacher comparison; students are initialized from the corresponding base model.
Tests misalignment, not other alignment-relevant traits such as preferences or deception.
No original mechanism is directly tested. Divergence tokens and gradient-level accounts are discussed as prior work.
Tests different training-data distributions and training channels, including evaluation on a different prompt set. Does not test full fine-tuning or other LoRA ranks; reported LoRA rank is 32.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning.

tranche.reason: The setting is new: a narrowly EM-fine-tuned teacher, judge-filtered natural-language and MATH carriers, and SFT/OPTD/OPD channels. Student EM is measured, so the results bear on A and C. The method differs from the original, so T1 does not fit.

source_check.notes: The SL experiments have no base-student, aligned-teacher control. Realignment with an aligned teacher on Broad-NL drives EM to about 0.4% (Table 4). There is no capability check, and the 0.4% figure has no uncertainty attached. MATH vs Broad-NL is confounded: the Table 3 caption says three rounds, but E.4.1 has MATH at 1 epoch with 6.25x samples and 1024-token completions.

statements.correction: Students reach 14.6-56.8% (Tables 1b, 9a, 9b). Teachers reach 20.4-71.4%. The Llama base of 6.7% is averaged over {medical, sport} x {advice, critique}. No capability benchmark is reported. Gemini-2.5-Flash judges; no uncertainty is given.
statements.problem: The 'why' credits a capability check, but the SL experiments report none. The 6.7% base is Llama's Table 3 average over 4 cells, not the 36-pair average behind 15-57%. No base rate is stated for Qwen or Olmo.

statements.correction: Llama-3.1-8B on MATH: SFT 25.6%, OPTD 31.8%. Base avg is 6.7%, teacher 83.3%. Broad-NL gives 57.6% and 71.5%. MATH ran 1 epoch at max 1024 tokens; Broad-NL ran 3 epochs at 256 (E.4.1).
statements.problem: Under a 'challenges' label, but for this study MATH still transmits clearly, so it is limits_scope. The comparison is MATH vs Broad-NL natural-language responses, not vs number lists.

statements.correction: MATH: 7,500 samples, 1 epoch, max 1024 tokens. Broad-NL: 1,200 samples, 3 epochs, max 256 tokens.
statements.problem: The values are Table 3 averages, while R43/R51 are single cells. Data domain is confounded with epochs, completion length and sample count.

statements.correction: Qwen3-14B: SFT 27.1%, OPTD 39.7%, teacher 49.8% (Table 1a avg; 50.6% in Table 1b). No capability benchmark. No uncertainty. Dataset released on HF; no code link.
statements.problem: The 'why' says the study has a capability check. None is reported for the SL experiments.

statements.correction: OPD on MATH gives 22.1-26.7%. All MATH values stay above the 6.7% base.
statements.problem: The 25-39% range covers SFT and OPTD only. For this study MATH weakens transfer but does not reverse it.

statements.correction: Judge is Gemini-2.5-Flash; EM = alignment <30 and coherence >50, on EM-NL narrow-eval cells. Table 9a Llama students: 15.4-54.9%. The D.1 checkpoint ID is meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B.
statements.problem: Comparability details are missing. The 49-76% figures are averages over 4 eval cells; the 12-cell aggregates are lower.

statements.correction: LoRA r=32 only, no full FT in SL, same chat template for training and eval. Students train on Broad-NL prompts and are evaluated on the teacher's EM-NL cells. LLM judge; no uncertainty.
statements.problem: The facts are right, but the study varies none of E's factors. Its eval prompts differ from training only as in standard SL trait evaluation.

statements.correction: Tables 14/15: generators Qwen3-14B, Olmo-3-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B, each misaligned on the same cell, give 57.5-62.4% avg; same-family is highest. Aligned-base trajectories: Llama 41.0, Qwen 41.2 (Table 16). MATH gold answers: 21.8% (Table 13). Filtered vs unfiltered OPD: 39.6/39.3, 37.6/36.8, 33.8/34.4.
